title: Artifact trace index for runtime images and driver compatibility
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: As we run multiple runtime variants across hosted, dedicated and private deployments, it's become difficult to reliably map a container image tag to the exact set of artifacts needed for safe upgrades: SBOM, pinned CUDA/driver compatibility, kernel ABI notes, and the runtime's semantic version (including LTS channel mapping). This causes manual checks during rollouts and intermittent incompatibility breaks in Dedicated clusters.

Goal: Build a canonical Artifact Trace Index service and associated CI/CD hooks so that every released runtime image has a machine-readable mapping to: image digest, SBOM locator(s), required driver/CUDA stack (with minimum/maximum tested versions), the LTS channel (if any), signature metadata, and the release ticket/PR. The index should be queryable by digest, tag, and by compatibility query (e.g., "which images are compatible with CUDA 12.1 on Ubuntu 22.04").

Scope:
- Index model and storage for artifact metadata (immutable by digest).
- SBOM ingestion pipeline that attaches provenance (who/what/when) and verifies SBOM signatures.
- Driver/CUDA compatibility records with test-verified ranges and a link to driver SBOMs.
- API endpoints for lookup and a lightweight CLI to pin images in rollout manifests.
- Integration with rollout gates so the Console can block or warn on mismatches.
- Backfill script to index recent images and provide audit logs for LTS channels.

Non-goals: full dependency resolution for arbitrary packages (only runtime/container-level metadata), replacing existing SBOM generation tools (we'll consume their output).

Approach:
1) Design a simple, append-only index keyed by image digest. Metadata fields: image_digest, image_tag_aliases, sbom_uri, sbom_checksum, sbom_signed_by, cuda_stack: {min_version,max_version,tested_with_driver}, os_base, runtime_semver, lts_channel, release_pr, signed_at, signer_key_id, ingestion_timestamp.
2) Implement ingestion pipeline in Go as a small service that runs in CI (Github Actions) after image build step. The pipeline verifies SBOM signature, extracts CUDA-related packages, and writes to index store (Postgres table with JSONB metadata).
3) Add /v1/artifacts/lookup endpoints: by digest, by tag, and by compatibility query. Requests return the canonical SBOM URI (S3), signed metadata, and compatibility flags.
4) Console integration: add a pre-rollout validation step that queries the index for target image and compares required driver ranges against cluster-node driver versions. If mismatch, fail gate or create a soft-warning depending on rollout policy.
5) Backfill: one-off job to index last 90 days of runtime images and mark LTS candidates.

Success metrics:
- 100% of new runtime images published to index at build time.
- Rollout gate prevents at least 90% of driver-compatibility mismatches caught by CI previously missed.
- Reduced manual checks during Dedicated upgrades by 80% for release engineers.

Risks and mitigation:
- Inaccurate SBOMs: add SBOM signature verification and provenance check.
- Index drift: make ingestion atomic and immutable by digest; provide an admin-only correction path with audit trail.
- Performance: keep hot-index in Postgres and add Redis cache for tag->digest lookups.

Deliverables:
- Design doc with schema and API contract (linked below).
- Ingestion service and CI action.
- API service and minimal auth (service tokens).
- CLI command `rw-artifact pin` used by rollout manifests.
- Console gating hook and e2e tests.

Notes on versioning and LTS channels: We'll follow semantic versioning for runtime images and introduce a separate LTS label pattern (e.g., runtime-2.2.lts-2026). The index will map lts_channel to specific patched digests so customers can pin to channel rather than digest when appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: CI action added to image build pipeline to publish to index
SBOM signature verification mandatory for ingestion
API endpoints respond to digest and compatibility queries within 200ms P95
Console rollout gate consults index and blocks incompatible upgrades by default on Dedicated
